root_cause.text: In nft_tunnel_obj_destroy(), metadata_dst_free() was used to free the metadata_dst, which directly kfree()s it without considering the dst_entry refcount, allowing a use-after-free when packets still hold references via dst_hold().
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `metadata_dst_free(priv->md)` with `dst_release(&priv->md->dst)`, and the CVE description states: "nft_tunnel_obj_destroy() calls metadata_dst_free() which directly kfree()s the metadata_dst, ignoring the dst_entry refcount."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix improper deallocation of tunnel metadata destination by using dst_release to handle reference counting correctly.

intent_record.how: Instead of directly freeing the whole metadata_dst structure, now the dst_entry inside it is released, which properly decrements the reference count and frees the metadata_dst when the refcount reaches zero.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the added file, nft_tunnel_obj_destroy() uses metadata_dst_free(), which directly frees the metadata_dst without considering the dst_entry refcount. Meanwhile, nft_tunnel_obj_eval() calls dst_hold() on the same metadata_dst and attaches it to skb via skb_dst_set(), meaning packets can hold references. This mismatch causes a use-after-free when the tunnel object is destroyed while packets still hold references. The vulnerable construct is present in this initial commit.
